findings.title: [P1] Keep branch values out of the shell command
findings.body: `showBranch` now interpolates `branch` directly into a command string passed to `exec`, which runs it through a shell. Any caller passing a value like `HEAD; printf __INJECTED__` (or `HEAD && <cmd>`) gets the appended command executed; the removed `execFileAsync("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value literally as one argv element, so this is a direct command-execution regression introduced by the diff. It also silently breaks valid ref names containing shell metacharacters (e.g. `a$b` expands to `a`), so even benign inputs can resolve to the wrong ref or fail. No other in-repo callers exist today, but this is an exported API whose input now crosses into a shell.

findings.title: [nit] Remove the obsolete execFile setup
findings.body: After switching to `execAsync`, the `execFile` named import (line 1) and the `const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)` binding are no longer referenced anywhere in the file, leaving dead code that should be cleaned up alongside the switch. (No `tsconfig.json`/lint config exists in the repo, so this does not currently fail a build.)
